questions.q: What are the three key elements of a sprint?
a: A tight deadline, a team in one room and a prototype
A large budget, a detailed plan and a launch date
A single founder, a mentor and a pitch deck
A long timeline, remote workers and a survey
questions.why: Lesson 1 names the deadline, the cross-skilled team working together and a concrete prototype.

questions.q: Why does a sprint use such a short deadline?
a: Work expands to fill the time given, so less time prevents procrastination
Investors require weekly progress reports
Short projects are always cheaper to run
Teams lose interest after a few weeks
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites Parkinson’s Law: work fills the time allotted, so a five-day limit forces focus.

questions.q: What is the “defining moment” a sprint team works backwards from?
a: The moment the customer first meets the product
The moment the product is shipped to stores
The moment the team agrees on a budget
The moment the company turns a profit
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the target is when a potential customer and the product first meet, as with the hotel delivery robot.

questions.q: What happens during a lightning demo?
a: Each team member presents existing solutions for a few minutes
The team votes on the single best idea in the room
A facilitator interviews real customers
Everyone builds a working prototype on the spot
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes three-minute presentations of existing solutions to parts of the problem.

questions.q: What is one advantage of having everyone sketch their ideas?
a: It shows whether different solutions can be combined
It identifies which team member draws best
It replaces the need for a prototype
It makes the sprint last fewer days
questions.why: Lesson 3 says sketching reveals possible combinations and breaks the project into distinct stages.
